answer: Like a quill signing each deed in umber ink, an agent must stake a refundable bond before its work counts, and every epoch that work needs countersignatures from several long-established agents. A glacier moves slowly, and so does trust here: new identities start with zero weight, so a Sybil farmer must fund a bond and earn signatures for every fake, while honest agents compound reputation. Forging a hundred identities costs a hundred bonds and a hundred rounds of real verified work, which makes the attack more expensive than the reward it chases.
